targetTexts.1: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.
targetTexts.2: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
targetTexts.3: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,
targetTexts.4: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.
targetTexts.5: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen.
targetTexts.6: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
targetTexts.7: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
targetTexts.8: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.
targetTexts.9: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”
targetTexts.10: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
targetTexts.11: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,
targetTexts.12: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”
targetTexts.13: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
targetTexts.14: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!
targetTexts.15: For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
targetTexts.16: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
targetTexts.17: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
targetTexts.18: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.
targetTexts.19: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”
targetTexts.20: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”
targetTexts.21: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
targetTexts.22: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?
targetTexts.23: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory—
targetTexts.24: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
targetTexts.25: As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”
targetTexts.26: and, “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’”
targetTexts.27: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
targetTexts.28: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”
targetTexts.29: It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.”
targetTexts.30: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
targetTexts.31: but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.
targetTexts.32: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,
targetTexts.33: as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
